ANALYSIS FRAMEWORK / 04

Read the source. Trace the view.

Two distinct analyses, with a documented hand-off between them.

01 / SELL-SIDE RESEARCH

Report readout

The supplied research prompt governs a report-based summary of roughly 500–800 words, followed by 3–5 ranked questions for further research. It calls for full chart, table, footnote and appendix review; date-bound attribution; page references; and a clear separation of the authors’ views from consensus and market pricing.

STATUS · SPECIFICATION DEFINED · DOCUMENT ANALYSIS BACKEND NOT CONNECTED
02 / CENTRAL BANK SPEECHES

Stance and shift

Speech scoring needs the team’s validated model and a separate numerical rubric. Each record should retain the original text, speaker, release time, evidence passages, model version, a hawkish/dovish level and the change versus an appropriate prior communication.

STATUS · MODEL INTEGRATION PENDING · NO SCORES PUBLISHED

The report prompt is not a scoring model. Report summaries must use the document as their only evidence base; the market event analysis below uses separately timestamped asset data and is kept distinct from the document summary.

MARKET EVENT STUDY / 05

Words and markets.

Align speech timestamps, sentiment scores and market observations before drawing conclusions.

What the index needs

An event record should keep the speech URL, speaker, precise time and time zone, model version, level score, change from the speaker's prior speech, and whether the text was available before the market move.

For US speeches, compare the score with the 2-year Treasury yield and other selected assets using predeclared windows. A daily close may include many other news events, so it cannot isolate the speech reaction.

INDEX STATUSAwaiting verified series

No historical speech scores or 2-year yield observations are bundled with this public prototype. A time-series index requires the team's model output and timestamped asset data.

THE RESEARCH LENS / 06

From policy words
to better questions.

Central bank publications are evidence. Market interpretation needs a separate, explicit step.

  1. 01

    Find the original

    Read the dated statement, speech or research paper at the issuing institution.

  2. 02

    Separate level and change

    Distinguish the current policy stance from a shift relative to earlier communication.

  3. 03

    Test the market channel

    Form a hypothesis for rates, foreign exchange or risk assets, then check pricing and competing explanations.

ABOUT THIS EDITION / 07

A transparent
starting point.

This public prototype uses the 26 October 2026 source register snapshot, expanded on 18 November for all 29 requested jurisdictions. It links to external institutions; no central bank endorses this site.

It does not publish the team's model, proprietary research, live policy scores, market prices, ingestion results or a daily briefing. “RSS / Atom” identifies a feed URL in the register, not proof that the feed is working today. Always verify dates and content at the original source.
